div.div: ≈25 MB. This is what goes to the registry and runs in the cluster — a smaller image is a faster pull, a faster scale-up and a smaller attack surface.

div.div: A different image per environment, so staging never tested the artefact production runs. Any config change is a rebuild.

div.div: One image, promoted unchanged from staging to production. Only the mounted config differs.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 655px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Build once, run anywhere is not a slogan here — it is the reason the image must contain no environment. Say "the builder stage is thrown away and config is mounted, so the bytes that passed staging are the bytes in production."
